chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Mu'alla ibn Khunays who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out one night while it was drizzling, intending to go to the dwellings of Bani Sa'idah. I followed him, and something fell from him. He said, 'In the name of Allah, O Allah, return it to us.' I approached him, greeted him, and he said, 'Are you Mu'alla?' I said, 'Yes, I am your ransom.' He said to me, 'Search with your hand for whatever you find of something and bring it to me.' I found scattered bread, so I kept bringing him what I found until I found a bag of bread. I said, 'I am your ransom, shall I carry it for you?' He said, 'No, I am more deserving of it than you, but go with me.' We arrived at the dwellings of Bani Sa'idah and found a group of people sleeping. He began tucking a loaf or two loaves under the garment of each one of them until he reached the last one. Then we returned.
I said, 'I am your ransom, do these people know the truth?' He said, 'If they knew, we would cover them with dust.' And 'dughah' is salt.
Indeed, Allah did not create anything except that it has a custodian who guards it, except for charity, for the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, takes charge of it Himself.

And my father, whenever he gave charity, would place it in the hand of the beggar, then take it back from him, kiss it, smell it, and then return it to the hand of the beggar. This is because it falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the beggar, so I liked to handle what Allah, Exalted, had taken charge of.
Indeed, charity at night extinguishes the anger of the Lord, wipes out the great sin, and lightens the reckoning. And charity during the day yields wealth and increases lifespan.

Indeed, Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him), when he passed by the sea, threw a loaf of his food into the water. Some of the disciples said to him, 'O Spirit of Allah and His Word, why did you do this? It was your food.' He said, 'I did this so that a creature of the water might eat it, and its reward is with Allah, the Great.'

key_terms.الدُّقَّه: Salt (specifically fine salt used as a metaphor for dust/covering)
key_terms.رُوحَ اللَّهِ: Spirit of Allah (title for Prophet Isa)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of giving charity at night compared to the day?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* illustrates the Imam’s humility and the metaphysical status of charity, noting that Allah personally guards *sadaqah* unlike other blessings. It distinguishes the spiritual purification of night charity from the material prosperity of daytime giving, culminating in the example of Prophet Isa (AS) feeding sea creatures to demonstrate that even small acts of charity yield immense divine reward.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Ali b. al-Hussain al-Sa’dabadi from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from his father from Sa’dan b. Muslim from Mu’alla b. Khunays who said:

“Whenever my father used to give Sadaqah, he used to take it back from the hands of the beggar, kiss that Sadaqah and smell it and then return it to him. He used to do it so because Sadaqah goes into the hands of Allah before going into the hands of beggar. He used to say that I like to have in my hands too what Allah’s hands had held.
Giving Sadaqah in darkness reduces the anger of Allah and wipes greater sins. It makes accounting of deeds easier.
Sadaqah given during day causes abundance in wealth and life.

Once Isa Ibne Maryam passed by a sea. He dropped his food in the sea. One of his companions asked, “O Ruhullah! Why did you do so? It was your food, why did you drop it?” He replied, “I dropped it so that the marine creatures consume it. It carries a great reward in front of Allah.”
